body: The engine is already exercised headlessly — `blitz-test-harness` synthesizes input through the real event-dispatch pipeline with no window or GPU, and the WPT runner renders to CPU buffers; the seven_guis stand boots through it (`seven_guis::stand`) at a pinned viewport with its bundled font, every boot offline but the load page's, whose one stylesheet fetch the in-process stand-in `LoadNet` answers. escher builds on that: stable element ids (built — `DioxusDocument::element_id(s)`, the author's HTML `id`, else a path anchored at the nearest keyed element of the same component, else the element's component path; proven the same across a re-render, a remount, a fresh process and edits of the code around an element; every element an agent can act on is keyed, checked by `DioxusDocument::unkeyed_actionable`; and the id is carried on every element's accessibility node as AccessKit `author_id`), a semantic snapshot (its data model built — `DioxusDocument::snapshot`, every element the accessibility tree keeps as a node of id · role · name · state · bounds, each field from a reader the engine already had; its state proven per control through real input — enabled, checked, value and focused — with a password's or a file input's value read as the fixed mask `MASKED_VALUE`, and selected, pressed and invalid read from what the app states in its markup: the engine's builder writes them on the accessibility node from `aria-selected` · `aria-pressed` (or `aria-checked` on a checkable role, ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18) · `aria-invalid`, a third direct engine change for every document, ratified by the founder (2026-10-10), and the stand's flight booker and CRUD state invalid and selected — the stand states no `aria-pressed`, the flight booker's mode a `select#flight-type` whose options state its choice, and `accessibility_states` pins the pressed reading on a fixture; its text form built — `Snapshot::to_text`, one line per node nested by indent, every lean stand screen under the 10,000-byte `SNAPSHOT_TEXT_BUDGET` (the Cells screen the stand serves beside them passing it), returned to its caller in process and, through the command line, in a hosted `snapshot`'s answer, and a screen over the budget read in parts — `Snapshot::text_parts`, consecutive pre-order lines never split, the driver's `snapshot` taking an optional `part` (a whole number, 1 to `MAX_PART` = 1000) and answering one part's text with the closed counts `part` and `parts`, part 1 by default, a part past the last the empty text, a screen within the budget answering whole as before, proven on an over-budget fixture page in both layout modes, in process and through `serve_mcp` (a ratified boundary widening); its diff built — `Snapshot::diff`, a comparison of the snapshots taken before and after a step that names exactly the nodes added, removed or changed, by stable element id, and is empty for a step that changes nothing, proven on the stand in both layout modes — beside an engine change flag that now tells the truth, `has_changes` reading true from a tracked write until `take_changed_nodes` drains it; the driver's acting verbs return that diff), a driver session (built — `escher_driver::Session` holds one headless instance across commands, one process hosts it until it is stopped or has answered no request for its 30-minute idle expiry, and `start` · `attach` · `stop` · `call` drive it over a local socket that carries its lifecycle and its calls; the stand hosts its own through the `escher-session` binary; since 2026-10-19-session-recording a session whose launcher names a recording directory (`--record`, `Session::recording_into`) keeps its answered calls as one owner-only replayable check — the calls as they crossed, a masked `type` as one fixed stand-in, each answer a 64-bit digest and kept whole — masked as on every carrier, a shot's without its pixels, so the screens' ids, names, values, snapshot text, diffs, a lint's findings, a UI graph's names, closed flag words and booleans, and an actions answer's ids, owner ids, verb words, closed cause words and booleans at rest — read back strictly by `Check::from_bytes` and replayed through `Session::run` alone by `Check::replay`, which stops at the first step whose acceptance or kept answer differs, ratified by the founder (2026-10-19); the repository's own two scripted Counter checks committed under `tests/blitz-tests/checks/`, the one exception to owner-only, replayed by `stand_replay` and kept fresh by seven_guis `recording`), settle detection (built — `Harness::settle` runs every pass that is due and returns `Settled`, or `NotSettled` naming the busy class: render and layout driven to quiet, a load in flight reported at once and never waited on, a timer or an animation neither waited on nor advanced; `Session::act` runs one step on the held instance and returns once it has settled, a load in flight waited for up to `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time, settled again every 10 ms, no time moving on the held instance) and one still loading at the bound `NotSettled(Loads)`; proven on the stand's Timer and on minimal fixtures in both layout modes, and every acting driver verb returns only once the instance has settled), the driver's command and refusal schema (built — one verb table of fourteen verbs in three levels, `snapshot` · `click` · `type` · `press` · `advance` · `scroll` · `screenshot` · `lint` · `graph` · `actions` asked of the held instance, `start` · `status` · `stop` of the session and `help` of the tool itself, each with its argument and result shapes, a validation that turns a call into a typed command or a refusal before anything runs, and eight refusal causes each with a fixed remedy, all eight returned today (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); time on a held instance moves by `advance`, in milliseconds, and an acting driver command waits on a load in flight for at most `LOAD_WAIT` (5 s of wall time), `snapshot`, `screenshot`, `lint`, `graph` and `actions` waiting on none), act by id (built — `Session::run` runs a call on the held instance: `click`, `type` and `scroll` name their target by the stable id a snapshot lists, `type` replaces what its control holds (on a select, single or `multiple`, focused with no click, it chooses the first option whose label starts with the text, on a `multiple` select its match alone), `press` acts on what holds focus, `advance` moves the session's clock — the harness's `VirtualClock` every harness-built document reads — by exactly `ms` on every session and the app's own time through the step the session's caller supplies where there is one (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), and each returns once the instance has settled, with the diff of the screen before and after; proven on the four lean stand tasks in both layout modes — the Timer's range input moved by `click` and the arrow, `Home` and `End` keys since the range interaction model, a direct engine change for every document ratified by the founder (2026-10-13), the diff naming the slider's `value` and its display's `name`, and, since the keyboard harness, `press enter` and `press space` on a Tab-focused button each counting as its click — keyboard activation, a direct engine change for every document ratified by the founder (2026-10-13)), refusal detection (built — an id the screen does not read is refused `stale` when an earlier screen of the session read it and `not-found` when none did, and a `click` or a `type` on a target that reads not enabled, lies out of view or is covered by another element is refused `disabled`, `off-screen` or `covered`, in that order, with nothing run and the instance unchanged; `scroll` brings its target into view through every scrolling box that holds it, a row of an open select list by writing that list's `scroll_y` alone — the engine's `scroll_into_view`, widened for every document on the founder's ratification — and says in its result whether it then is; proven on the stand and on minimal fixtures beside it, in both layout modes), driver command spans (built — every call handed to `Session::run` leaves one `tracing` span holding fixed words and counts only: its verb, a refused call's cause, an acting call's settle reading and the lengths of its diff; escher's sink prints it as one line per closed span, a record class ratified by the founder (2026-10-09), who ruled with it that a diff's content never reaches a log while its three sizes may; proven on the stand in both layout modes, with no id, name or typed text in the capture), the driver's command line (built — every driver command as one run of a binary that boots apps: `escher_driver::command_line`, a closed argv reader over the one verb table, a call checked before any session is touched, one uncoloured line of JSON on stdout and exit `0` accepted · `1` refused · `2` usage · `3` session error, nothing the caller typed written back; the stand's is the `escher-session` binary, whose `start` spawns its own host; proven on the six served tasks by the binary run as a process and by two flows scripted in plain `sh`), scrolled-box bounds and hit (built — a box that is itself scrolled reads its own `bounds` where it stands, and a hit stops at the padding box of every box that clips by `overflow`, both fixed in the engine for every document on the founder's ruling; a hit also stops at a `contain: paint` box (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); three readings are still off and said by the tool itself — a box clipped on one axis stops a hit at its whole padding box, so a target beside it along the axis it does not clip is refused `covered` though it shows, a box with no width or no height is hit at its centre on the element that holds it, so it can read `covered` though nothing covers it, and under a rotation a box's visible part reads as the bounding box of its rotated padding box, so an element in a corner it does not show can read in view — and the second position reader, `Node::absolute_position`, subtracts only its containing blocks' scroll offsets (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18); a box both transformed and scrolled is hit where its rows show, and `BaseDocument::get_client_bounding_rect` reads an element where its transforms move it (ratified by the founder, 2026-10-18), so a driver `click` on a translated button is accepted and lands), the MCP surface (built — `escher_driver::serve_mcp`, the driver's fourteen verbs as MCP tools over stdio, run by the `escher-session mcp` role an MCP client spawns, local to the invoking user with no listener or auth surface: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 in four handshake revisions, `2025-11-25` answered to any other since the self-description, a `snapshot` result the screen text itself for a whole screen and its JSON line `{"text","part","parts"}` for a paged one, an accepted `screenshot` an `image` block then a text block, and every other the JSON line, protocol errors fixed and running nothing, bounded at a 65,536-byte request line and a 1,048,576-byte result — one holding an image by its whole written form — with the request id echoed only in two forms — a crossing ratified by the founder — and each tool call one `tool_call` span holding `tool` and `ending`, the parent of its `command` span; proven on the stand in process in both layout modes, through the binary as a child under both builds, and once by a real client in a live trial, whose first request, `server/discover`, the server answers `-32601` and whose `initialize` asked `2025-11-25`, answered `2025-06-18` — a reading taken before the server spoke `2025-11-25`), the driver's self-description (built — `help`, the fourteenth and last verb, asked of the tool itself on the command line and over MCP and answered with no session run: `describe()`'s one line of JSON written from the tables alone — the verbs, the node keys each with its help, key names, busy classes, refusal causes and session errors each with its remedy, and the exit statuses — the program's own fixed text riding the ratified carriers, ratified by the founder (2026-10-12); every MCP tool described with its result fields, and a changed node in a returned diff naming the keys whose reading differs, `differs`), and the headless screenshot (built — `Harness::screenshot` / `screenshot_rect` paint the viewport with no display into `VelloCpuImageRenderer` over opaque white, and the driver's `screenshot`, the seventh instance verb on the command line and over MCP, returns the screen or one element's visible part as a PNG — no step, nothing changed, an app with no `sans-serif` family refused `fonts-unavailable` — its pixels in band, base64 in the answer line and an MCP `image` block, ratified by the founder (2026-10-12); a password input paints masked in every document, an engine change ratified by the founder (2026-10-12); proven on the stand in both layout modes, a whole shot an 800 × 600 PNG equal to the harness's raster and byte-identical across processes on one host — a shot's PNG bytes differ between linux x86_64 and macOS aarch64, so a check compared byte for byte across OSes holds no `screenshot` step), and the visual lint (built — in process and as the `lint` verb, the eighth instance verb, on every carrier and recorded, a ratified boundary widening — `Session::lint` reads the held screen for six defects, `overlap` · `clipped` · `truncated` · `off-screen` · `zero-size` · `contrast`, through blitz-dom's read-only `BaseDocument::text_extent` and `Harness::text_contrast`, and returns `Finding`s of ids, closed words and numbers, changing nothing, and carried by the `lint` verb — `Outcome::Linted`, written `{"findings":[…]}`, an MCP tool and a recorded step, its answer kept whole, its `command` span recording `verb` and, refused, `cause` alone; proven on a planted fixture page and on the stand in both layout modes, the counter, the flight booker, the timer, CRUD and the load page reading 0 findings at boot (the snapshot giving a closed select's options its client rect and the lint's `overlaps` skipping them, a `multiple` select's rows reading their own client rects and linted as usual, an open list's rows reading their own bounds in the list and `overlaps` skipping them too, a highlighted row's contrast unread) and the last CRUD row after twelve Creates reading `clipped` inside `crud-list`; a node both clipped or off-screen and holding text also reads `truncated`, pinned by `stand_lint` in both layout modes), and the select list (built — a single select opens a list the engine paints over the page by a click, by Enter, or by a Space with no typed text standing, a direct engine change for every document, remote pages included, ratified: one `BaseDocument` field `select_list`, answered first in `hit_with_scrollbar` and painted by `paint_scene` after the root's render, a row's own `bounds` crossing in the snapshot and the diff and an option's and a group's label leaving as pixels in a `screenshot`, a ratified boundary widening, with no new carrier, exit, cause, session error, node key, log field or span; proven headlessly in both layout modes by `select_popup`, `select_popup_painted` and `stand_act_popup` and through the host and the `mcp` role, what an assistive technology reads of it unmeasured and the windowed list read and not run), and the UI graph (built — `DioxusDocument::graph`, read-only, one node per snapshot node with its owner, component, handlers and reads, and the registered states an app declares through `use_graph_state`, each write flagged `undeclared` or `unconfirmed` where it is; the `graph` verb, the ninth instance verb, answers it whole and unpaged on every carrier and in a kept check — ids, names, closed flag words and booleans, never a value, a ratified boundary widening — and each snapshot node carries the closed bool `clickable`; proven on the stand in both layout modes by `stand_graph`), and handler coverage (built — `handler_coverage` replays kept checks, each on a fresh session, and lists the UI graph's handlers no check exercised, read through dioxus-native-dom's reached record, switched on for it alone; the `escher-session coverage <app> <check>...` role prints that coverage line — ids, owner ids, event names and two counts — on stdout, a ratified boundary widening; proven on the six served tasks in both layout modes by `stand_handler_coverage`), and seeded randomness (built — a run's randomness comes from one seed held as a Dioxus root context, ungated by the accessibility feature, `Harness::from_vdom` providing the default seed 0 where the builder gives none, so two runs of one seed read the same state at every step, in both layout modes and across processes, proven by `stand_seeded_randomness`; no seed crosses the driver's carriers, so every driver session and every kept check's replay reads the default seed — provisional, the founder's to confirm).
